name: Route registry (single source of nav truth)
purpose: One TypeScript list that decides what every navigation surface shows: rail, fly-outs, mobile drawer, landings, breadcrumbs, Cmd+K and search.

elements.name: ADMIN_ROUTES
elements.does: About 100 entries (workspace, label, icon, description, roles, section, keywords). Fewer than half of the ~197 page.tsx files; the rest are records, sub-pages or redirects.

elements.name: showInRail:false
elements.does: Hides a route from rail surfaces but keeps it in Cmd+K. Used on 56 rows.

elements.name: parked:true
elements.does: Hides a route from the rail AND search while keeping the URL alive. Used on 2 rows (pay progression).

elements.name: requiredBundle
elements.does: SaaS subscription gate. Declared on 3 rows only.

elements.name: scoreRoute / rankRoutes
elements.does: Fuzzy scoring behind Cmd+K.

elements.name: breadcrumbTrail
elements.does: Resolves breadcrumbs from the same list.

behaviours: Role gates are copied by hand from middleware.ts and AdminSidebar, then asserted equal by a test (header says it mirrors them).
Feature toggles are applied in accessibleRoutes so the four nav surfaces cannot disagree.
Workspace membership is a field on the route, so moving a page between workspaces changes every surface at once with no URL change.
problems: Three lists must agree and are kept in sync by tests, not by construction: the registry, the middleware ROLE table and each page's own check. An 2026-08-30 audit counted 135 page files; today there are 197.
56 of ~100 rows are showInRail:false, so the rail row count says little about how many pages exist.
Descriptions are long owner-quote essays in comments; the product copy itself is short and fine, the code is hard to scan.
AdminRoute has role lists and bundle gates but no concept of tabs; tabs live in a second generated file (lib/admin/portal/tabs.generated.json).
rebuild: Keep one registry, but make it generate middleware rules and the tab list instead of mirroring them: each destination declares {id, label, area, roles, tabs[], bundle}. Add a per-firm override layer (name, order, hidden) so a firm can rename 'Knowledge' or drop 'Equipment' without code.
add: Per-firm renaming and ordering of destinations
nationwide: Workspace names, labels, descriptions and keywords are Starr's vocabulary (e.g. 'Knowledge', owner quotes in descriptions). Registry is compiled in, so a firm cannot reorder or rename it. Bundles exist (SaaS) but only 3 rows use them.

name: Icon rail, fly-outs and the seven workspaces
purpose: The desktop navigation: a narrow rail of seven workspace icons (Hub, Work, Equipment, Research & CAD, Knowledge, Money, Office) with fly-outs listing each workspace's pages.

elements.name: Rail icons
elements.does: Seven workspaces with Mod+1..7 shortcuts (registry WORKSPACES).

elements.name: Fly-out
elements.does: Lists the workspace's rail-visible pages the user's roles and the firm's toggles allow.

elements.name: Pinned pages
elements.does: Starred pages from the page header are pinned to the rail (help-catalog tip, personas header).

elements.name: Persona reorder
elements.does: A persona (field-surveyor, equipment-manager, dispatcher, bookkeeper, researcher, admin, student) only reorders the rail; it never hides a workspace.

behaviours: Persona is inferred from role and can be overridden in the Hub greeting.
Equipment workspace has 4 registry rows, Research & CAD 5, so two of seven workspaces are nearly empty (PAGE_CONSOLIDATION section 12 records Equipment as a one-link anomaly).
Mobile uses AdminSidebar as a drawer, not the rail.
problems: Seven workspaces for a typical firm is too many to learn: counts by registry row are hub 11, work 18, equipment 4, research-cad 5, knowledge 12, money 15, office 21.
Knowledge is a workspace but has no landing in the consolidation write-up (section 12 table), and Learn + Knowledge + Exam Prep + Manage + Students all sit in it.
Office is a grab-bag (files, design studio, brand, people, comms, support, settings, reports, notifications): 21 rows in four sections.
rebuild: Collapse to four destinations that match how a firm talks: Today (hub), Jobs (field, schedule, equipment, CAD, research), Clients and Money (leads, contacts, calls, invoices, payments), Office and Learn (people, files, settings, how-to). Keep the rail but make each fly-out a short two-level list. See office.md section 'The admin shell'.
add: Per-firm choice of which workspaces appear
Role presets that pick the rail, not just reorder it
nationwide: 'Research & CAD' and 'Equipment' assume a firm that runs its own research and gear ledger; both should be optional modules. Persona names assume a Starr-sized crew.

name: Workspace landing pages (/admin/work, /office, /research-cad, /money)

elements.name: Stat strip
elements.does: Counts from /api/admin/workspace-summary. A count the server could not take is omitted, not shown as zero.

elements.name: Cards
elements.does: One per route in the workspace; Money and Office group by section.

behaviours: Office sections: Documents & records, People, Talking to people, Setup & account.
Equipment and Learn use their own landing rather than WorkspaceLanding.
problems: Landings repeat what the fly-out already lists; a user can reach the same page three ways (rail, landing card, Cmd+K).
Office is the only landing carrying 21 destinations; sections help but it is still a menu of a menu.
rebuild: Drop the landings as separate pages; put the same stat strip and top actions on the Hub for that persona, and let the fly-out be the directory.
add: 'What needs me in this area' count with a link, per workspace
nationwide: None specific.

elements.name: Pages

problems: Only six actions; no 'new lead', 'new contact', 'log a call', 'send email' action even though those are common office jobs.
Records are not searched here: the Search Everything page does that separately, so there are two searches.
rebuild: Make Cmd+K the one search: pages, actions and records (jobs, customers, leads, calls) in one ranked list, with the full results page behind 'see all'.
add: Actions for each office job (new lead, add contact, send email, find a call)

name: Roles, persona and the three-layer access model
purpose: Decides who sees what: 12 roles, a middleware prefix table, per-route registry roles, SaaS bundles and the firm's toggles.

elements.name: ALL_ROLES
elements.does: admin, developer, teacher, student, researcher, drawer, field_crew, employee, guest, tech_support, equipment_manager, finance.

elements.name: Middleware ROLE table
elements.does: Prefix to roles. /admin/settings, /payroll, /roles, /calls, /leads, /marketing are admin only; /design is admin+developer; /messages and /discussions are eight roles.

elements.name: Registry roles
elements.does: Mirror of the above for nav (shell-route-registry).

elements.name: API checks
elements.does: Each route repeats its own isAdmin or session check.

behaviours: Four different questions are kept apart on purpose: may you (roles), did the firm pay (bundle), is it for staff (internalOnly), does the firm use it (toggle).
Role builder exists (W7) for custom roles; scope not verified.
problems: There is no party-chief, drafter, RPLS or office-manager role. 'admin' is everything: leads, calls, marketing and settings are admin only, so an office manager has to be given full admin to use the CRM.

Middleware and API disagree in places: /admin/discussions is open to eight roles but POST and PUT /api/admin/discussions are admin only (discussions route:65,172), so non-admins can open the tab and the floating Report button but not post.

GET /api/admin/contacts only checks sign-in although its header says admin (contacts route:28); PAGE_CONSOLIDATION section 13.2 records that any signed-in account, including a student, can read the client list.
Finance role is additive and was added late (2026-08-12); office permission still hangs off admin.
rebuild: Use permissions by capability (view leads, send quotes, read call recordings, approve hours, manage settings) bundled into editable role templates (Owner, Office manager, RPLS, Party chief, Drafter, Field tech, Bookkeeper). Generate middleware and nav from the same table.
add: Role templates a firm can edit
nationwide: Role names are Starr's seven-person crew model (drawer, field_crew, researcher). Roles are global constants, not per-organisation.

name: Page toggles (switch pages on or off per firm)
purpose: Lets the owner hide pages and tabs the firm does not use so the menu is shorter. Visibility only, never a permission.

elements.name: Toggle map
elements.does: Stored as exceptions only in the app_settings key feature_toggles: absent means on.

elements.name: Keys
elements.does: A route, or route#tab for a tab of a portal.

elements.name: Pages tab
elements.does: One switch per destination, grouped like the sidebar, each saves immediately and reverts on failure.

elements.name: isDestinationEnabled
elements.does: A tab of a switched-off portal counts as off.

behaviours: Read by sidebar, rail, palette and search; the redirect sends a visitor away from a switched-off page.
A test asserts APIs answer the same with a page off.
problems: Non-admins get an empty destinations list (feature-toggles route:127), so the toggle screen is admin only while the toggles apply to everyone: right, but the firm has no way to say 'hide for crew only'.
Toggle keys are route strings; renaming a route silently orphans a toggle.
It treats a symptom: 197 pages exist so firms need a switch to hide them. Fewer pages and modules would remove the need.
rebuild: Replace page-level toggles with modules chosen at onboarding (Jobs, CRM and leads, Phone receptionist, Marketing, Learn, Research, Equipment, Payroll). Toggle by module; keep the per-page switch as an advanced option.
nationwide: Already per firm (org-scoped app_settings row). Defaults assume a full Starr-style install.
